title: Coloured signs
html_source:
A reference to a theory on light of Bishop Cloyne George Berkeley.

The Bishop of Berkeley was an immaterialist/ subjective idealist. He believed material mass and objects only exist because of the minds which perceive them. An early theory on light expressed this philosophy.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: With this intellelectual supposition, one might suppose there be a need to oversimplify perception or possibly overemphasize a specific set of perceptions as a means of engaging veritable ‘proofs’ associated with indepth analysis. The stuff of footing an ivory tower?

Is this the point at which pragmatists are drawn to the faiths of unknowing as both students and seekers adamant regarding their need for some leader or vision which organizes the profusion of nature?

I am reminded of the film ‘Being There’ with Peter Sellers where he becomes the attache of prominent men by adhering strictly to his limitations as they fawn on his oversimplified understanding of the natural world. Its complexity and verity to form allow his isolated observations to apply adeptly to his followers derivations of understanding as their perception allows. His simple nature further does nothing to contradict their belief that he has a profound understanding of their adapted permutation to suit the path they perceive.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: ‘Coloured’ because after Aristotle, colour is what allows determined non-transparent bodies to be seen (from the 1922 Text notes – Oxford University Press )
